description: Nigerian-origin customers abroad report refusals and closures with no stated ground, because stating one may constitute tipping off. There is no accusation to rebut.
energy_note: Declined, permanently, with no charge stated.

description: Every subsequent institution sees a closed account and applies its own caution. One unexplained closure produces a pattern that then justifies itself.
energy_note: One closure, and then all of them.

aspect: Business banking is where it bites hardest
description: A merchant account, a payment processor, a business current account. Without these there is no company, regardless of the customers, the revenue or the product.
energy_note: Allowed to trade, not allowed to bank.

description: The mechanism is the same one recorded for Iranians and Palestinians: a compliance decision taken about a nationality, executed against an individual, with no route of appeal. Only the country name changes.
notes: Cross-reference: FIN category in assets/text/iran and assets/text/palestine.

description: Two founders, a UK company, a signed contract with a Manchester client. The bank declines the business account. No reason is given, because giving one may constitute tipping off. They try three more banks over five months, then register the company in Estonia instead.
energy_note: A real company, banked in a country neither founder has seen.

aspect: It selects who gets to build anything
description: The founders who survive this are the ones with a relative abroad, a second passport, or enough capital to wait five months. The constraint does not filter for the best businesses; it filters for the best-connected ones, and then the outcome is read as a comment on Nigerian enterprise.
energy_note: A filter on connections, mistaken for a filter on merit.
